name: Cockayne Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Cockayne Syndrome

criteria.description: Postnatal growth failure with short stature and failure to thrive
Marked photosensitivity with sunburn reaction and pigmentary changes
Progressive neurological deterioration including developmental delay and sensorineural hearing loss
Features of premature aging including cachectic appearance and loss of subcutaneous fat
Defective nucleotide excision repair demonstrated by cellular assays

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (growth failure, photosensitivity, neurological degeneration) with supportive genetic or cellular evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing confirming mutations in ERCC6 or ERCC8 genes supports diagnosis

common.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities including cataracts and pigmentary retinopathy

occasional.symptomName: Feeding difficulties and failure to thrive

laboratory: Defective DNA repair assays (reduced recovery of RNA synthesis after UV exposure)
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Calcifications in basal ganglia and white matter abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in ERCC6 (CSB) or ERCC8 (CSA) genes
other: Characteristic facial features including sunken eyes, thin nose, and micrognathia

distinguishingFeatures: Severe photosensitivity with skin cancer predisposition
Lack of neurological degeneration in some subtypes

redFlags: Severe photosensitivity with minimal sun exposure
Progressive neurological decline in infancy or early childhood
Failure to thrive with characteristic cachectic appearance
references: Nance MA, Berry SA. Cockayne syndrome: review of 140 cases. Am J Med Genet. 1992;42(1):68-84.
Kraemer KH, et al. Cockayne syndrome and xeroderma pigmentosum: DNA repair disorders with overlapping clinical features. DNA Repair (Amst). 2007;6(7):1026-1035.
Lehmann AR. Cockayne syndrome: the expanding clinical and mutational spectrum. Mech Ageing Dev. 2003;124(1):1-7.
